title: Bounded construction of a tail field
statement: Let $m,k$ be nonnegative integers, let $	ext{src}$ and $	ext{dst}$ be distinct indices in $	ext{Fin}(m)$, let $w$ be a finite word over an alphabet $93$, and let $	ext{last}$ be an alphabet symbol. Form the word $F$ by joining $k$ copies of $w$ followed by the one-symbol word $[	ext{last}]$, with a blank separator between consecutive words. Suppose a configuration $d$ on a fixed input is in the prescribed entry state, the source tape contains the word $w$ at each offset $p$ with $-1\le p\le |w|$ (using blank cells outside the word), and the destination tape is blank at each offset $p$ with $-1\le p\le |F|$. The constructed machine reaches its prescribed exit state at some time $t\le (k+1)(4|w|+12)$ and is not in that state at any earlier time. At every time $u\le t$, each work-tape head is at distance at most $|F|+1$ from its initial position; at time $t$, the configuration agrees with $d$ except that its state is the exit state and the destination tape contains $F$ from its initial head position onward, with all other cells and tapes unchanged.
